lines.en: Hello, Mia. What seems to be the problem today?
lines.pt: Olá, Mia. Qual parece ser o problema hoje?

lines.en: I’ve had a headache all day, and I’ve felt dizzy since breakfast.
lines.pt: Estou com dor de cabeça o dia todo e me sinto tonto desde o café da manhã.

lines.en: I see. Have you had a fever, or a cough?
lines.pt: Entendo. O senhor teve febre ou tosse?

lines.en: I’ve had a cough for two days, but I haven’t had a fever.
lines.pt: Estou com tosse há dois dias, mas não tive febre.

lines.en: Have you taken any medicine since yesterday?
lines.pt: O senhor tomou algum remédio desde ontem?

lines.en: Yes, I’ve taken two tablets, but my throat has been sore since Monday.
lines.pt: Sim, tomei dois comprimidos, mas minha garganta está dolorida desde segunda.

lines.en: How long have you had this sore throat exactly?
lines.pt: Há quanto tempo o senhor tem essa dor de garganta exatamente?

lines.en: For about four days. I’ve worked a lot this week, so I’ve slept badly.
lines.pt: Há uns quatro dias. Trabalhei muito esta semana, então dormi mal.

lines.en: That explains it. Your body has needed rest for a while.
lines.pt: Isso explica. Seu corpo precisa de descanso há algum tempo.

lines.en: I’ve wanted to stay home since Tuesday, but I’ve had many meetings.
lines.pt: Quero ficar em casa desde terça, mas tive muitas reuniões.

lines.en: Please rest, drink warm tea, and come back if you’ve had a fever by Friday.
lines.pt: Descanse, beba chá quente e volte se tiver febre até sexta.

facts.big: I’ve had it for two days
facts.label: Present perfect com for e since
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio com for + período e since + momento: I’ve had a headache all day. Pergunte com How long have you…?

facts.label: Há + tempo
facts.sub: Use for com um período: for two days, for a week, for a long time. I’ve had a cough for two days. É assim que você diz há quanto tempo o sintoma dura. Depois de for, nunca use um dia da semana.

facts.label: Desde + momento
facts.sub: Use since com um ponto no tempo: since Monday, since breakfast, since 2019. I’ve felt dizzy since breakfast. Pense em “desde quando” e no começo do problema.

compare.ask: I’ve had a cough for two days.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “estou com tosse há dois dias”, no presente.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’ve had a cough for two days.”
compare.us: Em inglês, usamos o present perfect: I’ve had a cough for two days. Com um ponto no tempo, usamos since: since Monday.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use for with a period of time.
items.why: For two days, for a week.

items.s: We use since with a point in time.
I’ve had a cough since two days.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use for with a period of time. → Verdadeiro (For two days, for a week.)
We use since with a point in time. → Verdadeiro (Since Monday, since breakfast.)
I’ve had a cough since two days. → Falso (Say for two days.)

pages.title: A small clinic in Toronto · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey morning in Toronto. Noah has been at work since early Monday. He has had a headache all day. Now he is in a small clinic. Nell, the nurse, has worked here for ten years. She wants to know how long he has felt ill.
“Hello, Noah. What seems to be the problem today?” says Nell. “I’ve had a headache all day, and I’ve felt dizzy since breakfast.” says Noah. “I see. Have you had a fever, or a cough?” says Nell.
